subject: Next steps: Dedicated capacity sizing call (Nimbus Analytics)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Dedicated capacity sizing call (Nimbus Analytics)

Hi Samir — great to connect earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Goal: understand Nimbus's production inference profile so we can size a dedicated Redwood pool (throughput, concurrency, and latency SLOs).
- Key constraints you mentioned: 99th P95 latency sensitivity for interactive chat, bursty batch scoring in evenings, and compliance requirement for regional isolation.
- Attendees for the sizing call: Marissa (AE), Priyom (Solutions Engineer), Dev (Infra). Please feel free to add anyone from your infra/ML team.

To keep momentum, can we schedule a 60-minute capacity-sizing session next week where we go over:
1) your traffic profiles and peak windows
2) target latency and throughput per model/endpoint
3) test data and benchmark plan
4) recommended hardware/config and follow-up action items

Proposed slots (PT):
- Fri 5/29 10:00–11:00am PT
- Mon 6/1 9:00–10:00am PT
- Mon 6/1 1:00–2:00pm PT

I've attached a short capacity sizing template to fill (redwood_capacity_sizing_template.xlsx) — if you can send the populated sheet or a quick export of your observed QPS/concurrency and typical sequence lengths before the call, that will help us run real estimates during the meeting.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning calendars.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood_capacity_sizing_template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@nimbus-analytics.com>

Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Dedicated capacity sizing call (Nimbus Analytics)

Thanks Marissa — appreciated the recap. We'd like to move quickly on this. The 5/29 10am PT slot works for our team (Lena, our ML infra lead, will join).

Preliminary production numbers (high-level):
- Peak sustained QPS: ~120 requests/sec (chat completion endpoint)
- Typical request size: 512 tokens (avg), max 1024 tokens
- Concurrency target during peak: ~30 concurrent sessions
- Latency SLO: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms for interactive chat responses
- Batch scoring: nightly batch jobs hitting ~2k requests/min for shorter inputs (avg 64 tokens)

I'll attach our export of the last 7 days (nim-scaling-data.csv). If you need anything else ahead of the call (model names, quantized weights, or dataset examples) let me know and I'll pull them.

See you Friday.

—Samir
Director of Engineering | Nimbus Analytics
samir.shah@nimbus-analytics.com
Attachment: nim-scaling-data.csv (CSV stub)
